insights.text: This is a genuinely two-platform show: 57% of all actual watching happens on X broadcasts (12,710 of 22,436 total views), not just YouTube with an X echo.
insights.recommendation: Give X broadcasts first-class treatment — real titles, thumbnails, and call-outs, not simulcast leftovers.
insights.caveat: Per-episode X share ranges 46% (E1 (Bumpy Takeoff)) to 72% (E3 (Mixed Media Workflows)); only episodes with complete X play counts are included (6).

insights.text: People actually sit in @ridd_design's room: 62% of broadcast watching happens there (5,303 ridd vs 3,201 tom).
insights.recommendation: If the split holds, make @ridd_design's account the flagship broadcast and use @designertom's for clips and reposts.
insights.caveat: Episodes where both hosts' plays are known, with promo outliers left out (5).

insights.text: @ridd_design's announce posts travel further on X — 57% of announce impressions (18,784 ridd vs 14,148 tom).
insights.recommendation: Lead each announcement from @ridd_design's account and have @designertom quote-post it — order the announce machine around what actually travels.
insights.caveat: Reach = exposure, not watching, and is never charted or summed with views. Promo outlier excluded; small sample (5 episodes) — read as tendency.

insights.text: Announce hooks close very differently: E4 (Backyard Designers behind-the-scenes) turned 41 of every 100 announce impressions into actual plays; E5 (Goodbye) managed only 23.
insights.recommendation: Reuse E4 (Backyard Designers behind-the-scenes)'s announce format — more of the people who saw that post chose to watch. High reach with few plays means the post traveled but didn't sell the click.
insights.caveat: X broadcast plays for every 100 announce impressions; episodes at least 7 days old, with promo outliers left out, sample of 4.

insights.text: E3 (Mixed Media Workflows) is a promo-driven outlier, not a topic winner: more than double what a typical episode gets (4,206 X plays vs a typical 1,836; 19,633 X reach vs a typical 7,164).
insights.recommendation: Don't copy this episode's topic because of its numbers — separate the paid/promo lift from organic pull first.
insights.caveat: Outlier = more than double the typical episode on that unit; excluded from host-split aggregates automatically.

insights.text: E1 (Bumpy Takeoff) pulled the most engaged viewers — 49.7 likes+comments per 1,000 YouTube views; E3 (Mixed Media Workflows) the least at 30.
insights.recommendation: Mine E1 (Bumpy Takeoff)'s comments for what hooked people — that topic drove interaction, not just plays.
insights.caveat: YouTube only; episodes at least 7 days old because likes and comments per 1,000 views change with age, sample of 5.

insights.text: The Mascot Industrial Complex + Live Call-Ins drew a live peak of 71 concurrent viewers (avg 50) — #2 of 6 episodes, against a typical peak of 64.
insights.recommendation: Turnout held up — keep the same time slot and announce rhythm.
insights.caveat: Peak concurrents from Restream across all simulcast destinations; compared with the typical result from 5 prior episodes.

insights.text: Live chat is down from launch: 383 messages on the first show, 127 on the latest.
insights.recommendation: Chat is the call-in pipeline — seed prompts and questions mid-show instead of waiting for organic chat.
insights.caveat: Message totals from Restream chat archives, all destinations combined.

insights.text: E3, E4 and E5 were registered late — their early weekly history doesn't exist. Totals are right; first-week growth comparisons aren't.
insights.recommendation: Nothing to do — the flags are automatic. Just don't read first-week growth comparisons for these episodes.
insights.caveat: Tracked late: E3 (Mixed Media Workflows), E4 (Backyard Designers behind-the-scenes), E5 (Goodbye). Marked "tracked late" in the episode panel.
